newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa arrivals sluggish in June.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa arrivals sluggish in June.

text.p: Ivorian cocoa has been dribbling into ports at a rate of 5-7,000 tonnes a week since mid-May but July is expected to propel volumes towards a mid-crop (May-Sept) forecast range of 150-180,000 tonnes, industry sources said on Thursday.

One set of data shows 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) cocoa arrivals totalling 1.033 million tonnes by May 25, around seven percent or 70,000 tonnes down on the record 1995/96 season, when Ivory Coast yielded 1.2 million tonnes, port sources said.

Another set of more recent data put arrivals to June 13 at around 1.04 million tonnes after arrivals in the preceding week totalling around 6,500 tonnes, said one source, putting total deliveries to factories at about 118,000 tonnes.
Arrivals by June 16 last year totalled 1.13 million tonnes, sources said.
Analysts are waiting until August to put a figure to forecasts for the 1997/98 main crop (Oct-April).
